chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Yahya al-Lahham, from Sama'ah, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)

Regarding a man who married a free woman and for him is a slave wife, and the free woman did not know that for him is a slave wife. He (peace be upon him) said: 'If the free woman desires to stay with the slave wife, she stays; and if she desires, she goes back to her family.'

I said to him: 'If she is not pleased with that and goes back to her family, is there a way for him upon her when she is not pleased with staying?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'There is no way for him upon her when she is not pleased when she comes to know.'

I said: 'So her going back to her family is her divorce?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'Yes. When she goes out from his house, she observes a waiting period of three months or three menses-free periods, then she marries if she desires.'

key_terms.سَبِيلٌ: Authority/way (specifically the husband's right to keep her)
key_terms.قُرُوءٌ: Menstrual periods (used to calculate waiting period)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling for a free wife if her husband has a slave wife and she chooses to leave?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi elucidates the concept of *Khiyar al-Nafadh* (option of separation) for a free wife upon discovering her husband's concurrent marriage to a slave girl, a ruling rooted in the preservation of her social status (*kafa'ah*). It clarifies that her voluntary departure from the marital home constitutes an irrevocable divorce (*Talaq*) rather than a mere separation, mandating a specific *Iddah* period of three months or three menstrual cycles before she may remarry, reflecting the jurisprudential nuance between free and enslaved women in Shia fiqh.

en.hubeali: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Yahya Al Lahaam, from Sama’at,

(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> regarding a man who marries a free woman and for him is a slave wife, and the free woman does not know that for him is a slave wife. He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘If she so desires to, she can stay with the slave girl with a staying, and if she so desires to she goes back to her family’.

He (the narrator) said, ‘I said to him<sup>asws</sup>, ‘Supposing she is not happy with that and she goes back to her family, is there a way for him upon her when she is not happy with the staying?’ He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘There is no way for him upon her when she is not happy when she comes to know’.

I said, ‘So she goes back to her family, he has (been deemed to have) divorced her?’ He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Yes. When she goes out from his house, she would observe the waiting period of three months, or three menses-free periods, then she can marry (someone else) if she so desires to’.
en.sarwar: 4. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Mahbub from Yahya al-Lahham from Sama‘ah who has said the following:

“About the case of a man who marries a free woman and he has a wife who is a slave-girl and the free woman does not know that he has a slave-girl wife, abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘If the free woman wants to live with his slave-girl wife, she can do so and if she wants she can go to her family.’

I then asked, ‘If she did not like to live with his slave-girl wife and went to her family, is there a way for him to bring her back?’ He (the Imam) said, ‘He has no way to bring her back if she does not agree when she finds out.’

I then asked, ‘Is her going to her family her divorce?’ He (the Imam) said, ‘Yes, when she goes out of his house, she commences her waiting period for three months or three cycles of menses then she can marry if she so chooses.’”
